subtitle: Lesson 4 · Modeling a real three-tier application

code:
Order Tracking Application (customer-facing)

  Web server    -- public-facing site
  App server    -- business logic
  DB server     -- order + customer data

Task: pick the right cmdb_ci subclass for each piece.
caption: A standard three-tier web application, worked on paper.

code:
cmdb_ci_appl
  name: Order Tracking Application
  version: 4.2 | vendor: in-house | criticality: high

cmdb_ci_server x2
  WEB-HARROW-01   cpu:4  ram:16GB  os:Ubuntu 22.04
  APP-HARROW-01   cpu:8  ram:32GB  os:Ubuntu 22.04
caption: Two servers = two separate CIs, each independently trackable.

code:
cmdb_ci_server          cmdb_ci_database
  (hosts the engine)       (the data + schema)
  DB-HARROW-01       !=    Harrow Orders DB
  OS, CPU, RAM              db_type: PostgreSQL
                            schema: orders_prod

Server can reboot without the instance changing, and vice versa.
caption: Two separate CIs — collapsing them loses independent tracking.
